headline: Britannia's sea remembers the rain
lede: The weather fronts that drift over Britannia now leave their mark on the water: rain and storms wind the swell, and the sea keeps heaving for epochs after the sky clears. Storm crests gain stroke, shore foam thickens, big crests break whitecaps — and a sea clear for four epochs is bit-exactly the calm water it always was.

notes.text: seaRough wind-memory: precipitation over the last four epochs lifts each tile's sea state (weights 1 / 0.5 / 0.24 / 0.11), pure render math — the sim, its hashes and the proven constant-speed drift are untouched.

Proof: britanniacheck 205/205 with two mutants (zero the memory -> exactly 3 red; pin the gains -> exactly 2 red); a new real-key drive (britannidrive 10/10) watches the panel ride STORM 1.00 down through CLEAR 0.50 / 0.28 / 0.13 and proves the heaviest epoch paints more bright sea ink at the same seed.

This finished a corpse: the engine+gates were pushed by a warden-kicked session; this slot resumed per playbook and shipped mutants, the drive, and the README gap (#1 now PARTIAL — front speed stays honestly open).
First QA polish pass filed for BRITANNIA: sea-state as ship hazard, splash sound, constant-speed fronts, and an ART.md look review.
